questions.question: Cell phones can seriously distract drivers.
questions.explanation: While driving, do not use cell phones, computers, or other distracting devices. The only exceptions are reporting a crash or emergency. Keep your full attention on the road.

questions.question: Octagonal signs mean you must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is red with white letters and has an octagon shape. When you see a stop sign, come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or line. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to possible dangers ahead. This sign tells you the right lane is ending and traffic may merge.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, wait until the entire car is visible in your rearview mirror before moving back to the right lane.
questions.explanation: When passing, do not return to your original lane until you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car needs more distance to stop and may skid on turns. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Reduce your speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A yellow triangular sign with black letters means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of two-lane roads where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: If you have an argument and feel angry, you should:

options.text: Play loud radio music while driving to avoid thinking about it.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to release your anger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect how safely you drive. If you are angry, excited, scared, worried, or sad, calm down before driving. You need to focus completely on the road.

questions.question: If you drive faster than others on a two-lane road and pass many cars, you will:

options.text: Get to your destination faster and safer.
Increase your chances of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Every time you pass a vehicle, your risk of a crash increases.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry, you should:
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, distance yourself from them physically and mentally. Do not make eye contact or use hand gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever is safe to stay out of danger.

questions.question: Is smoking while driving a distraction?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving.
No, it helps keep drivers alert.
No, it is not a distraction.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This creates a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a roundabout is coming. Enter the roundabout slowly and let traffic already in the roundabout go first.

questions.question: Which factor commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving too fast or faster than the speed limit.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast or faster than the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions cause many accidents. Always drive at a safe speed and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and take out the key.

questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle, you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Which statement is true about bad weather?

options.text: Sudden weather changes mean you need to change how you drive.
You should slow down when it rains or is foggy.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather. They may be driving too fast.
All of the above are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above are true.
questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Also watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for conditions.

questions.question: Which is against the law?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle at a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass on hills, curves, at street crossings, at railroad crossings, in marked no passing zones, or where a solid yellow line is on your side. Do not pass in work zones or when the car ahead has stopped for a pedestrian.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both your side and rearview mirrors. Then quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people inside.
Some lanes are for specific turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people inside.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. It is reserved for buses and vehicles with the driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you drink only a little.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired by alcohol is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely if you drink alcohol or use drugs. It puts you and everyone on the road at risk.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving right away.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs together can strengthen each other's effects. Driving after alcohol or drugs is dangerous. Driving after both together is even more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that wet roads are slippery and dangerous. You can lose control of your car. Slow down on wet pavement because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close behind another car):

options.text: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Stops other cars from cutting you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous behavior that can lead to aggressive driving. You may face legal consequences for unsafe driving.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol level (BAC) goes up, you become:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the amount of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: You cannot follow an emergency vehicle with its siren on within ____ feet.
questions.explanation: Give space to ambulances, fire trucks, police cars, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. It is illegal to follow within 500 feet of an emergency vehicle responding to an emergency.

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb because:

options.text: You only need to signal if other cars are nearby.
It is a good habit and required by law.
You only need to signal during the move, not before.
You don't need to signal if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a good habit and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal your intentions well before you turn or change lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving left or right. Always signal before leaving a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly whenever you drive.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Check for injuries and call 911 if needed. Report the crash to police if anyone is hurt, someone died, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: Orange signs are used in construction work zones.
questions.explanation: Most work zone signs are orange and diamond-shaped. Some are rectangular. These signs are reflective so drivers can see them at night.

questions.question: White pavement markings (solid or dashed) separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
